record.notes: The Roderick D. MacDonald Research Fund is a Baylor St. Luke's Medical Center endowment, administered through BCM's Office of Research IT page, that awards up to $50,000 for one year with five review deadlines annually (2026: Jan 7, Mar 9, May 7, Aug 7, Nov 9). It is open to BSLMC professional staff and associated investigators, and explicitly to clinicians from other institutions whose collaborative project involves St. Luke's staff and is conducted at BSLMC or an affiliate, so a BCM breast medical oncologist practicing at Baylor St. Luke's is a natural applicant. For the PI it is the quickest local source of seed money for a ctDNA/MRD or EHR pilot, a biomarker sub-study nested in an existing trial, or start-up costs for an investigator-initiated trial. The trap is sequencing: the committee will not consider a proposal until a St. Luke's-accepted IRB (Baylor, BRANY, UT or CHI) has already approved the protocol, so the IRB submission must precede the fund application by months, and the budget cannot carry indirects, travel, publication costs or more than $10,000 in salary. The committee gives highest priority to work with clinical application to the quality or safety of care for hospitalized BSLMC patients, so an outpatient breast biomarker project should articulate a concrete care-delivery payoff at St. Luke's. Applications are delivered on paper to the committee chair and the BSLMC Office of Research (Neurosensory Building, 3rd floor). Next step: obtain IRB approval for the pilot protocol now and target the November 9, 2026 deadline; the committee normally meets within three weeks of each deadline.

record.eligibility: Applicants must hold an MD, PhD, DO, PharmD or equivalent doctoral degree, be US citizens, nationals or permanent residents, and be employed by a domestic nonprofit or government entity. New applicants must have total qualifying educational debt equal to or exceeding 20 percent of institutional annual base salary at award (waived for renewals) and must commit to an average of at least 20 hours per week of qualified clinical research during each quarterly service period; NIH research funding is not required. Qualified research is patient-oriented research with human subjects, epidemiologic, behavioral, outcomes or health-services research, which covers EHR, ctDNA/MRD and registry work. Ineligible are those with a federal judgment lien, an unresolved health-professional service obligation, federal employment over 20 hours per week, any research support or salary from a for-profit organization, or current IRTA/CRTA awards; only one LRP application per fiscal year is allowed.
record.notes: The NIH Extramural Loan Repayment Program for Clinical Researchers (LRP-CR, L30) repays up to $50,000 per year of qualified educational debt for doctoral-level investigators who commit to at least 20 hours per week of clinical research at a domestic nonprofit or government employer. The FY2027 notice NOT-OD-26-081 (released July 13, 2026) confirms the cycle opened September 1, 2026 and closes November 19, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EST, with awards starting between July 1 and September 30, 2027. It matters to the PI because there is no career-stage cap, NIH funding is not a prerequisite, and EHR, ctDNA/MRD and registry work fits squarely within NIH's definition of clinical research; it is disease-agnostic, so breast or ER+/HER2+ relevance carries no weight in review. The award is personal debt relief rather than research money, so it should be treated as a salary-support complement, not a project grant. The trap is the two hard gates: the PI must still carry educational debt of at least 20 percent of base salary at the time of award, and must be able to document, quarterly, a 50 percent research effort while holding clinical duties; a breast oncologist at 30 percent protected time cannot certify this. A further trap is the exclusion of anyone receiving research support or salary from a for-profit organization, which the PI should reconcile against industry consulting and industry-sponsored trial arrangements. Next step: confirm remaining debt balance and base salary, confirm protected research time is at least 50 percent, then register in the LRP portal, line up the mentor or institutional contact and the BCM business official certification, and submit before November 19, 2026.

record.eligibility: Any researcher may submit a data request through the Vivli platform; the administrator check confirms that all required form fields are complete and that "a qualified statistician is part of the team." record.notes: Vivli is a data-sharing platform, not a funder: a request yields individual participant-level data from contributed industry trials in a hosted secure research environment, with no money attached. It matters to the PI because Daiichi Sankyo, AstraZeneca, Pfizer, Novartis and Lilly are listed members, which is the route to pooled or secondary analyses of the DESTINY-Breast series and HR+/HER2+ registrational trials for questions on HER2 heterogeneity, ADC sequencing and endocrine resistance, i.e. the computational and translational angles. Requests are rolling; the process is an administrator completeness check (which requires a qualified statistician on the team), a contributor feasibility review, and an independent review panel judging scientific merit, followed by training and a non-negotiable DUA executed by BCM. The trap is treating this as a funded award or assuming any specific trial is available: ClinicalTrials.gov entries naming Vivli do not guarantee the contributor will release the dataset, and contributor-specific policies (timing after publication, endpoints, regulatory approval status) were not verifiable from the platform pages. A second trap is cost: the Standard environment is free for 365 days but bills $12/day thereafter, so analysis plans should finish within a year or budget the overage. record.award_text: Not a funding award. Access to banked, non-reserved biospecimens and annotated clinical/outcome data from completed phase 2/3 and phase 3 NCTN trials (Navigator inventory described as over 2 million to 3 million specimens). Investigators receive a feasibility assessment and cost estimate; after CCSC approval they must document their own funding for Group biospecimen processing/shipping fees, data collection/processing fees, and laboratory work within 12 months or specimens return to inventory.

record.eligibility: Requests for NCTN biospecimens from completed NCTN trials may be submitted by investigators in the research community, not only members of the NCTN Groups. The proposal PI must be a CTEP-registered investigator in every submission format. Requests go through the NCTN Navigator (LOI for feasibility review, then a full CCSC Proposal Submission Form with letters of support including one from the study's primary statistician) or directly to the Group bank for trials not in Navigator; if any trial in a multi-trial request is in Navigator the whole request must go through Navigator. Approved projects must document funding within 12 months and publish all results, including negative ones.
record.notes: The NCTN Core Correlative Sciences Committee pathway is NCI's standing mechanism for obtaining banked specimens and outcome-annotated clinical data from completed phase 2/3 and phase 3 cooperative-group trials; it provides no money and instead delivers a feasibility assessment and cost estimate. For the PI it is the most direct route to trial-quality tissue and plasma from completed breast trials (Alliance, NRG, SWOG, ECOG-ACRIN) for HER2-heterogeneity, endocrine-resistance, ADC-response or ctDNA/MRD biomarker validation, and an approved CCSC project is a strong preliminary-access statement inside an R01, R21, DoD BCRP or K-level application. The trap is sequencing: CCSC approval releases nothing until funding is documented, and the 12-month clock starts at the approval letter, so the PI should either hold a funded award that can absorb Group processing, shipping and data fees, or time the LOI so a pending grant decision lands inside that window. The evaluation guidelines favor validation of locked prediction models and pre-specified predictive biomarkers with power calculations and false-discovery control, so exploratory discovery pitches score poorly. The PI must be CTEP-registered (routine for a clinical trialist at an NCTN member site) and must recruit the trial's primary statistician for a letter of support, which usually means engaging the relevant Group breast committee first. Next step is to browse the public catalog at nctnbanks.cancer.gov for candidate trials, then submit a Navigator LOI; proposals accepted at least six weeks before a standing review date are scheduled for that call, with decisions expected about two weeks after review.

record.eligibility: Applicants must hold an MD, PhD, DO, PharmD or equivalent doctoral-level degree, be US citizens, nationals or permanent residents, and be employed by and conduct research supported by a domestic nonprofit or government entity. New applicants must have total qualifying educational debt equal to or exceeding 20 percent of institutional annual base salary and must contractually commit to an average of at least 20 hours per week of qualified research for an initial two years; NIH research funding is not required and there is no career-stage or years-since-appointment cap. Research must fall within a FOCUS area designated by the sponsoring Institute, and NCI's FOCUS areas are data science, computational biology, informatics, prevention, cancer control and population sciences, and human-based approaches to cancer biology, diagnosis and treatment. Ineligible are individuals receiving any research support or salary from a for-profit organization, federal employees working more than 20 hours per week, current IRTA/CRTA recipients, and anyone with a federal judgment lien; only one LRP application per fiscal year is permitted.
record.notes: The NIH Extramural Loan Repayment Program for Facilitating Opportunities in Cutting-edge Science (LRP-FOCUS, L70) repays up to $50,000 per year of qualified educational debt for doctoral-level investigators who commit to at least 20 hours per week of research in an Institute-designated emerging or high-priority area. The FY2027 notice NOT-OD-26-083 (released July 13, 2026, replacing the former LRP-REACH notice NOT-OD-25-094) confirms the cycle opened September 1, 2026 and closes November 19, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EST, with repayment starting between July 1 and September 30, 2027. It matters to the PI because NCI's published FOCUS areas name data science, computational biology, informatics and cancer control and population sciences, which is a closer match to the PI's EHR, ctDNA/MRD and registry work than the generic clinical-research definition under LRP-CR, and there is no career-stage cap and no NIH-funding prerequisite. The award is personal debt relief, not research money, and is disease-agnostic, so breast or ER+/HER2+ relevance carries no weight in review. The trap is threefold: the PI must still carry educational debt of at least 20 percent of base salary, must be able to certify a 50 percent research effort quarterly while holding clinical duties, and may submit only one LRP application per fiscal year, so L70 and the held L30 (LRP-CR) are mutually exclusive rather than additive. A further trap is the exclusion of anyone receiving research support or salary from a for-profit organization, which must be reconciled against industry consulting and industry-sponsored trial arrangements. Next step: confirm remaining debt and protected time, then contact the NCI LRP scientific liaison to confirm that computational and real-world-evidence oncology fits NCI's FOCUS priorities and to decide between L30 and L70 before registering in ASSIST and submitting by November 19, 2026.

record.notes: RFA-RM-27-012 is the first-cycle Data-to-Model Academic-Industrial Partnership NOFO of the new NIH Common Fund PRIMED-AI program, a UG3/UH3 phased cooperative agreement (administered by NCI on behalf of NIH) to build AI-enabled, image-centered, multimodal clinical decision support tools headed toward Software as a Medical Device. Budgets run to $450,000 direct per year in UG3 and $800,000 direct per year in UH3 over up to five years, with roughly six to eight awards expected; applications are due 2026-10-19 with no letter of intent and no second receipt date. It matters to the PI because the disease-agnostic call explicitly names digital-twin CDS tools that fuse clinical imaging, genomic profiling, and real-world EHR and patient-reported data to model individual response trajectories, which is the PI's top computational and real-world-data angle; an HER2-heterogeneity or endocrine-resistance use case combining pathology or radiology images with ctDNA/MRD and EHR data is a credible framing, but breast cancer is not mentioned anywhere in the NOFO. With five weeks to the deadline and an industry MPI, leadership plan, IP terms, and milestone Gantt charts required, the PI should only pursue this cycle if an existing industry relationship and imaging-AI collaborator can be committed immediately; otherwise it is worth tracking for a possible reissue, since Common Fund programs typically run multiple rounds but this NOFO itself expires 2026-10-20.
